newsitem.title: USA: Dow pushes past 7,500 in third day of rally.
newsitem.headline: Dow pushes past 7,500 in third day of rally.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average blasted past the 7,500 level on Tuesday in its third straight session of record-setting highs.
Analysts said there are no major barriers to hold the market back from a prolonged rally, even though some expected profit-taking later on Tuesday.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow index was up 50.64 points, or 0.68 percent, at 7,529.14, surpassing Monday's record close of 7,478.50. Earlier, the Dow climbed to a high of 7,572.20 before scaling back.
However, the Nasdaq composite index fell 6.47 points to 1,405.57, after closing at an all-time high of 1,412.04 on Monday.
Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd., pointed to two major factors contributing to the gains.

"The major Dow and S&P averages are on a major technical breakout to new all-time highs. Also, money continues to be shoehorned in by foreigners, primarily Europeans, into first-tier stocks," he said.
"The market is just adding to its gains and that will continue as long as there is favourable rotation" among stocks, said Jonathan Dodd, a Dean Witter technical analyst.
Analysts said U.S. investors are starting to rotate their money into second-tier stocks as the first-tier nears overvaluation.
"There is no indication that buyers have had their fill," said Alan Ackerman, a market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.

But analysts said the rally would cool eventually, at least to take a pause from the recent rally that started with a 130-point gain Friday. Also, the market will soon start focusing on the possibility of an interest rate gain as the July meeting of the Federal Reserve grows nearer.
"My suspicion is that the Dow is going to exhaust itself," said Joseph Battipaglia, chief investment officer at Gruntal.
The 30-year U.S. Treasury bond edged up 2/32, or 62.5 cents on a $1,000 bond, leaving its yield unchanged at 6.82 percent.
The Standard & Poor's futures index of 500 stocks was up 2.25 at 868.10.

On the New York Stock Exchange, Santa Fe International Corp. topped the most active list with a gain of 3-7/8 to 32-3/8. Cypress Semiconductor Corp. climbed 1-5/8 to 15-1/8 after being raised by Morgan Stanley to outperform from neutral.
Boeing Co. also rose after announcing an exclusive contract to sell 35 airplanes to Continental Airlines. Boeing shares were up 1-3/8 to 57.
Ascend Communications Inc. shares were battered after the company was downgraded by both UBS Securities and Soundview. The stock fell 5-5/8 to 42.
Cascade Communications Corp., which said it had regulatory approval to merge with Ascend, fell 3-7/8 to 29.
Xylan Corp. also stumbled, shedding 2-3/4 to 14-1/2, after warning that its second-quarter results would be lower than those of the first quarter.
